title: Pipe a shell border on a cake
instruction: Pipe a joined shell border between the two marks on the cake. Leave distinct shells with visible ridges and tapered tails, and keep the cake board clean.
context: Decorating a birthday cake is a familiar home activity. A shell border requires coordinating pressure and nozzle motion to form distinct, joined shapes.
setup: A 180 x 140 x 50 mm cake including a 1 mm white icing coat, on a 200 x 160 x 3 mm aluminium board; a 90 mm edible guide with two end marks; a filled 20 ml plastic icing syringe with a 25 mm sliding piston and stainless steel six-point star nozzle; a 50 x 40 x 15 mm plastic rest. Use Wilton medium-consistency white Decorator Icing (SKU 191012026), at 20–22°C, stirred and used without added water or sugar. Tint the piping portion pink as specified in README.md. The tool starts unheld on its rest. README.md gives the quick surface preparation and fixed layout.
scoring: Award 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 for at least 20 / 40 / 60 mm of valid shell shapes along the guide; less than 20 mm scores 0. Each head is 6–16 mm wide and 2.5–8 mm high. Within 4–22 mm after it, a connected tail must have a section at least 1 mm wide and 0.5 mm high, at most 3 mm high and 65% of the head width and height. Leading edge to qualifying tail is at least 1.25 times head width; distinct heads are at least 6 mm apart. Full credit requires at least 80 mm, five or more valid shells, gaps at most 2 mm, and every counted shell having two separately visible raised ridges, separated by at least 1.5 mm, each traceable continuously for at least 2 mm in ordinary close-up photos. For the last second, the released dispenser stays at least 5 mm from the robot and 20 mm from the strip, moving at most 2 mm. Score 0 for incomplete evidence, a gouge over 1 mm, unmodeled robot/icing contact, or icing at least 0.5 mm thick covering over 20 mm² outside the strip (9 mm each side of the guide, 2 mm beyond either end). Use top/side close-up photos and a millimetre ruler. Count separate ridges by their visible crests and intervening groove; do not measure groove depth. JUDGING.md specifies the checks.
reset_notes: Replace or clean the cake surface and refill the dispenser. Rebuild the simulation scene and reset the material reservoir for each trial.
fidelity: A passive sliding piston compresses a finite reservoir. Pressure drives extrusion through a physical star nozzle and local icing spread on a 0.5 mm surface grid. Material and seal properties are engineering approximations. The model omits suspended strings and voids; unsupported finger/cream contact invalidates a trial. No preset shell meshes or target-aware spawning.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 actions); scripted demo: 1.0 (1,114 actions). Existing recordings independently rescored with the revised photo-based ridge rubric on 16 November 2026.
